name: First Aid Kit
description: TSA rules for flying with first aid kits, bandages, medical shears, and antiseptic liquids in carry-on and checked luggage.

carryOn.reason: First aid kits are allowed in carry-on bags. However, specific contents must comply with standard TSA regulations: liquid antiseptics must be 3.4 oz or less, and scissors/shears must have blades less than 4 inches from the pivot point.
conditions: Bandages, gauze, medical tape, wraps, and solid pills are fully allowed with no restrictions.
Antiseptic ointments, hydrogen peroxide, and rubbing alcohol liquids must be in containers of 3.4 oz (100ml) or less.
Trauma shears and scissors must measure less than 4 inches (10 cm) from the pivot point.
Scalpels, surgical razor blades, and large shears are prohibited in carry-on bags.
exceptions: Essential prescription medical items are exempt from 3-1-1 limits if declared.

checkedBag.reason: Complete first aid kits, including larger scissors, surgical tools, and full-size antiseptic bottles, are fully permitted in checked baggage.
conditions: Ensure any sharp instruments or shears are securely sheathed or wrapped.

tsa.pageTitle: Can I bring a first aid kit on a plane?

airlines.name: American Airlines
airlines.notes: Standard first aid kits permitted in cabin and checked baggage.

airlines.name: British Airways
airlines.notes: First aid kits allowed in cabin provided sharp objects meet blade length restrictions.

travelTips: Before packing a pre-assembled commercial first aid kit into your carry-on, inspect it for sharp tweezers, scalpel blades, or liquid bottles over 3.4 oz.
Pack common travel essentials: blister bandages, ibuprofen, antidiarrheal tablets, and rehydration salts in your carry-on for easy access in-flight.
Medical shears under 4 inches from the fulcrum pass TSA, but pack them visibly near the top of your bag.

faq.question: Can I bring a first aid kit in my carry-on bag?
faq.answer: Yes! You can bring a first aid kit in your carry-on bag. Just ensure that any antiseptic creams or liquid bottles inside are 3.4 oz (100ml) or less, and that any scissors have blades under 4 inches from the pivot point.

faq.question: Are trauma shears allowed in carry-on luggage?
faq.answer: Yes, if the blades measure less than 4 inches from the pivot screw. Most standard 5.5-inch and 7.25-inch medical trauma shears have blade lengths under 3 inches from the fulcrum, making them TSA-compliant for cabin luggage.

faq.question: Can I pack a full medical kit in checked baggage?
faq.answer: Yes! Full-size first aid and trauma kits, including larger shears, surgical tools, and larger bottles of antiseptic, are 100% permitted in checked baggage.
